title: Canna Oil Recipe: Fast Kief-Infused Olive Oil
metaDescription: A quick canna oil recipe: kief infused into olive oil in a sealed jar water bath with no straining, plus flower directions, potency math and safe storage.
excerpt: Kief takes a shorter steep than flower here, skips the straining and tastes cleaner, which makes it a natural match for olive oil you drizzle. Flower directions included.
keyTakeaways: Kief gets about 2 hours in a jar water bath and stays in the oil, so there's nothing to strain.
Ground flower works too: infuse it for 3 to 4 hours, then strain.
Grams × 1,000 × THC% is the ceiling, and a cup of oil holds 96 half teaspoons.
Use infused oil raw or at the end of cooking, never for frying.
Refrigerated, it keeps 4 days; freeze what you won't use by then in measured cubes, right away.
body:
This canna oil recipe uses kief, the resin-rich powder that collects under a grinder's screen, to make infused olive oil in about 2 hours. Kief leaves almost no leafy material behind, so there's nothing to strain and less grassy flavor. Flower works too, with a longer infusion and a strain at the end.

## Kief or flower: which to choose

Kief suits a finishing oil for bread, salads or [canna-pesto](/blog/super-green-canna-pesto/) and is stronger by weight; flower suits bigger batches. Our guide to [what kief is](/blog/what-is-kief/) covers collecting it, and our [canna oil guide](/blog/canna-oil/) compares other methods.

## Dosing: estimate mg per half teaspoon

Grams × 1,000 × THC% is the most THC your oil can hold, spread across the 96 half teaspoons in a cup. One gram of kief labeled 40% THC gives 400 mg, about 4 mg per half teaspoon at most. Kief from your own grinder has no label, so assume it's strong. Try a quarter teaspoon by itself and let at least 2 hours pass before you cook with more. For starting amounts, see our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/).

## What you need

- 1 cup olive oil or another oil
- 1 gram kief, or 3.5 grams ground flower, decarbed
- A canning jar with a lid, a saucepan deep enough to submerge most of it, and a cooking thermometer
- Cheesecloth, for flower only

You can order flower ahead from [your local High Society store's menu](/shop/) for pickup.

## The canna oil recipe, step by step

Kief scorches easily, so decarb it in a thin layer at 240°F for about 30 minutes and keep an eye on it; flower takes 30 to 45. Seal it in the jar with the oil, rest the jar on a towel in the saucepan and add water to the oil line. Keep the water just under a simmer, 180 to 200°F: about 2 hours for kief, 3 to 4 for flower. Vent once, halfway through. Kief oil is ready as is, while flower oil gets strained while warm.

## Picking the oil

Infused oil stays off high heat, so choose by flavor:

| Oil | Flavor | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Extra-virgin olive | Fruity, peppery | Drizzling, dressings |
| Avocado, canola or sunflower | Mild | Baking, gentle sautés |
| Coconut | Mild; firms when chilled | Baking, coffee, canna-honey |

## Storage and labeling

The CDC says to refrigerate homemade oils made with herbs and toss them after 4 days, and University of Georgia Extension notes that a dried herb doesn't make the oil safe on its own. So keep only what you'll use within 4 days in the fridge, and freeze the rest in cubes right away. Write "infused," the date and the mg per half teaspoon on the jar, and park it where children and pets can't reach.

faq.q: What is kief and where does it come from?
faq.a: Kief is the pile of tiny, resin-filled trichomes that shake loose from dried cannabis flower. It collects under the screen of a grinder with a kief catcher. Because it's mostly trichomes, the glands where the plant makes and stores THCA, the source of its THC, it typically packs more THC per gram than the buds it fell from, so go by the label's THC figure when there is one.

faq.q: Can I make canna oil without straining?
faq.a: Yes, with kief. It leaves so little plant material that the oil can go straight into a jar; just stir before you measure, since fine specks can settle. Flower is different. Its leafy bits turn the oil bitter and gritty, so strain it through cheesecloth while it's still warm.

faq.q: How long does canna oil last?
faq.a: Four days in the fridge, which is the limit the CDC sets for homemade herb oils, and much longer frozen. Freezing it in measured cubes is the easy route: each cube carries a known estimate, and you thaw only what a recipe needs. A cupboard is never the place for homemade infused oil.

sources.label: Wang M. et al., Decarboxylation Study of Acidic Cannabinoids, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research (2016)
CDC: Botulism Prevention (homemade oils made with garlic or herbs)
University of Georgia Extension, Circular 1334: How to Safely Make Infused Oils (2024)
Colorado State University, Kendall Reagan Nutrition Center: Cooking with Fats and Oils (2019)
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)

ingredients: 1 gram kief (or 3.5 grams cannabis flower, coarsely ground)
1 cup extra-virgin olive oil or another oil
steps: Preheat the oven to 240°F. Spread the kief in a thin layer on parchment in a small baking dish and bake about 30 minutes, checking that it doesn't scorch (flower: 30 to 45 minutes). Cool it.
Scrape the kief into a canning jar, pour in the oil and screw the lid on finger-tight.
Rest the jar on a folded towel in a saucepan and pour in warm water to the height of the oil.
Keep the water just under a simmer, about 180 to 200°F, for 2 hours (flower: 3 to 4 hours), adding hot water as it evaporates.
At the halfway point, lift the jar with oven mitts, crack the lid open briefly to vent, swirl and set it back.
Cool the oil until warm. Kief oil needs no straining; pour flower oil through cheesecloth.
Mark the jar with the day you made it and its estimated strength. It keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze any extra in measured cubes.
recipe.dosingNote: Estimate only: 1 g of kief labeled 40% THC holds at most 1 × 1,000 × 0.40 = 400 mg, about 4 mg per half teaspoon across 96 half teaspoons. With 3.5 g of 18% flower, it's 630 mg, about 6.6 mg per half teaspoon. The kief's real potency, plus losses in the oven and the water bath, decide the true number, which will usually be lower. Try a quarter teaspoon on its own before cooking with it, and let at least 2 hours pass. Write the strength on the jar and on anything you make with it, and shelve both where kids and pets can't get them.

claims.claim: Kief is the resin-rich powder of trichomes that collects under a grinder's screen
claims.source: Moreno-Sanz 2016, Cannabis Cannabinoid Res (PMID 28861488): 'THCA-A is biosynthesized and accumulated in glandular trichomes present on flowers and leaves'; Romero et al. 2020, Plant Sci (PMID 32771172): cannabinoids share 'the same biosynthetic compartmentalization (i.e. glandular trichomes of leaves and flowers)'. Abstracts via NCBI E-utilities, 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Kief is stronger by weight than the flower it came from
claims.source: Follows from the trichome localization above (a sifted trichome fraction carries less non-glandular tissue); no fixed potency is stated, and readers go by the label.

claims.claim: FAQ: kief is 'mostly resin'
claims.fix: Kief is sifted trichomes (gland heads and stalks plus some plant dust), not resin as such. Now 'mostly trichomes, the glands where the plant makes and stores THCA, the source of its THC'.
claims.source: Moreno-Sanz 2016; Romero 2020.

claims.claim: Kief 'infuses faster than flower' / 'infuses in about 2 hours' (excerpt and takeaway)
claims.fix: No measurement of kief-versus-flower infusion speed was found. Reworded as the recipe's own timing: 'takes a shorter steep than flower here' and 'gets about 2 hours'.
claims.source: Search 2026-10-24 found only vendor and blog material on kief.

claims.claim: Kief leaves almost no leafy material, so nothing to strain and less grassy flavor; flower needs straining
claims.source: Method and sensory description; the FAQ tells readers to stir before measuring because fine specks settle.

claims.claim: Ceiling = grams x 1,000 x THC%; a cup holds 96 half teaspoons; 1 g of 40% kief = 400 mg, about 4 mg per half teaspoon
claims.source: Arithmetic (1 cup = 48 tsp = 96 half tsp; 400/96 = 4.17). The 40% figure is framed as a label example.

claims.claim: Dosing note: 3.5 g of 18% flower = 630 mg, 'about 6.5 mg' per half teaspoon
claims.source: Arithmetic.

claims.claim: Dosing note: the true number 'will be lower'
claims.fix: Now 'will usually be lower': the ceiling uses a label THC% that Michigan rules let vary by 10%.
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-labeling (R 420.504(1)).

claims.claim: Let 2 hours pass before more (body and dosing note)
claims.fix: Now 'at least 2 hours' in both places.
claims.source: CCMOH statement, Public Health Agency of Canada (Jan. 6, 2020): 'up to 4 hours to feel the full effects'. Opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: Try a quarter teaspoon by itself first (about 2.1 mg of the kief example)
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: start with 2.5 mg of THC or less.

claims.claim: Decarb kief in a thin layer at 240 F for about 30 minutes (flower 30 to 45); kief scorches easily
claims.source: Wang et al. 2016 (PMC5549281, full text via Europe PMC): THCA-A 'approached zero in 30 ... min at 110 C' (230 F) in extracts; the scorch warning is a kitchen caution.

claims.claim: Water bath just under a simmer, 180 to 200 F; about 2 hours for kief, 3 to 4 for flower; vent once halfway
claims.source: Method; a bath below a simmer stays under the boiling point.

claims.claim: Infused oil stays off high heat; use it raw or at the end of cooking, never for frying
claims.source: Wang 2016: THC peaked within 5-10 min at 145 C (293 F) then fell, and CBN formed at 160-180 C; frying runs about 350-375 F.

claims.claim: Oil table: extra-virgin olive for drizzling and dressings; avocado, canola or sunflower mild; coconut firms when chilled
claims.source: Colorado State University KRNC, 'Cooking with Fats and Oils' (Anita Bancroft, April 2019, opened 2026-10-24): EVOO for 'salads, dressings & marinades or ... a finishing oil'; avocado, canola and sunflower rated high heat. Coconut oil is solid at fridge temperature: Food Chemistry: X (2026), PMC13277645, full text via Europe PMC read 2026-10-24, measured melting points of 25.25 C (77 F) for virgin and 26.86 C (80 F) for refined coconut oil.

claims.claim: CDC: refrigerate homemade oils made with herbs and toss them after 4 days
claims.source: CDC Botulism Prevention (Feb. 26, 2026): 'Refrigerate homemade oils made with garlic or herbs. Throw the oils away after 4 days.'

claims.claim: UGA Extension: a dried herb doesn't make the oil safe on its own
claims.source: UGA C1334 (Dec. 17, 2024): using dried garlic and herbs 'still does not ensure that your ingredients are dried enough to provide a safe product'.

claims.claim: Takeaway: 'Refrigerated, it lasts 4 days; after that, freeze it'; body: 'anything beyond that goes into the freezer'
claims.fix: Freezing is the alternative to the 4-day fridge limit, not a step after it (CDC: throw it away after 4 days). Now: freeze what won't be used within 4 days, right away.
claims.source: UGA C1334: 'discarded 4 days after being made. Alternatively, you could freeze the oil'; CDC Botulism Prevention.

claims.claim: FAQ: four days in the fridge, much longer frozen, never the cupboard
claims.source: CDC and UGA C1334 as above.

claims.claim: High Society: order flower ahead from your local store's menu for pickup (kief not claimed)
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering; flower is a published category; no kief or product stock is claimed (brief mustAvoid).

claims.claim: Sources resolve and support the text
claims.source: Wang 2016, CDC, UGA C1334, CSU KRNC and CCMOH all opened 2026-10-24.

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 20 claims checked, 6 fixed ('mostly resin', 'infuses faster', 6.5 to 6.6 mg, 'will be lower', wait time, freeze-after-4-days sequence). Sources unchanged.
review.writerNotes: Brief suggested cupboard storage short-term; replaced with fridge (4 days) or freezer per CDC and UGA guidance for homemade herb oils, matching /blog/canna-oil/. No claim that High Society sells kief (mustAvoid); the store mention covers flower only. Kief described as stronger by weight than its source flower (concentrated trichomes); no typical potency stated. Jar steps worded differently from /blog/canna-butter-recipe/.
